# v1.1.0-dev.77 — The windows list becomes a table

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.76`.

Sixteen changes, most of them things you can see.

## The Windows List Is A Table

**App & title · Monitor · Desktop · Edit · ×**, and that's it. The
geometry that used to crowd every row moved into a card that appears
when you hover one:

- a picture of where that window sits, drawn to scale on your actual
  monitor layout, with nothing else on it
- its resolution
- its position, and which monitor that's on
- whether it's normal, minimised or maximised

The reorder grip is still there, in the title cell, appearing when you
hover the row.

## Pick A Colour For Any Window

The edit dialog has a colour well. It opens showing the colour the
window is already drawn in — the one generated from the app name — and
picking a new one changes it on the Visual tab and in the hover card.
**Reset** puts it back.

## The Profile List Moves

Drag its right edge to resize it, double-click that edge to go back to
the default, and collapse it entirely with the arrow in its header. A
button appears at the left edge to bring it back. Both the width and
the collapsed state are remembered.

## Windows Remember Where You Put Them

The app window and every dialog remember their size and position and
come back to them next launch. Each *kind* of dialog remembers its own,
because they aren't interchangeable — the settings dialog wants to be
wide and a confirm doesn't.

A remembered position is only used if it still lands on a display that
exists, so unplugging a monitor can't restore a window somewhere you
can't reach it. **Settings → Diagnostics → Reset window positions**
clears the lot.

## Dialogs Know What Size They Can Wear

Every dialog now declares the size its own layout needs and refuses to
be dragged smaller. The ones that are a fixed amount of content have a
ceiling too — stretching a yes/no confirm across a 4K display isn't
bigger, it's one sentence adrift in a field of background.

The **Set hotkey** dialog was the worst offender in the other
direction: it was inheriting the fill-the-window sizing, so a box
asking for one key combination was the size of the app. It's the size
of what it's asking for now.

## Keyboard

- **j/k wraps** at both ends, in both panes.
- Moving through the profile list now **shows that profile on the
  right** as you go. It's a preview, not a load — no windows move.
- The **selection marker** in the windows list was rendering a stray
  lowercase "a" down the left of the selected row. It's a pink chevron
  and a bar now.
- The **focused-pane outline** showed white and got covered by list
  rows. Both are fixed, and it's pink.

## Inputs And Dropdowns

One treatment across the app: consistent borders, a focus ring, and a
custom chevron on every dropdown instead of the platform arrow.

## Settings

- The left-hand tabs all fit on one line. "Companion software" was
  wrapping onto two.
- **Companion software** can now check whether the tools you already
  have are out of date, and run the update. Both go through winget.
  Each installed entry gets its own **Update** button, and there's a
  **Check for updates** button that asks about all of them at once.

## Windows, Edges And Shadows

Rounded corners and the drop shadow are asked for explicitly on both
the app window and every dialog rather than left to a default. The
outline squares itself when the window is maximised, which is what
"sometimes missing its border radius" was.

Clicking the app while a dialog is open now flashes the dialog. That
one needed a different approach than you'd expect: the app window is
genuinely disabled by Windows while a dialog is up, which is what makes
it modal — and a disabled window receives no mouse messages at all, so
there's nothing to listen for. The button is polled instead, only while
a dialog is actually open.

## The Display Editor

The arrangement always opens showing what Windows currently has. Now it
says so — and when you move something, it says **Changed from your
current arrangement** and offers **Revert**.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
